structured_output.summary: The diff changes `avg()` from dividing by `len(xs)` to dividing by `len(xs) - 1`. That breaks the function: it no longer returns the mean for any input. A one-element list now raises ZeroDivisionError. An empty list gives -0.0 or 0.0 where it used to raise. The name `avg` and the plain `sum` numerator mean this is not a deliberate sample-variance (Bessel) correction. The change should be reverted.

findings.title: avg() divides by n-1 and no longer returns the mean
findings.body: calc.py:2 now computes `sum(xs) / (len(xs) - 1)`. For xs=[2,4,6] it returns 6.0 instead of 4.0, and every non-empty input of length 2 or more gives a result inflated by n/(n-1). Dividing by n-1 (Bessel's correction) is only right for sample variance or standard deviation of squared deviations. It is never right for the arithmetic mean. Any code that calls avg() will get wrong results without any error.
findings.recommendation: Change it back to `return sum(xs) / len(xs)`. If a sample-variance helper was the goal, add a separate function, e.g. `def sample_var(xs): m = avg(xs); return sum((x - m) ** 2 for x in xs) / (len(xs) - 1)`.

findings.title: Single-element input now raises ZeroDivisionError; empty input returns 0 without an error
findings.body: With `len(xs) - 1`, avg([5]) divides by 0 and raises ZeroDivisionError, where it used to return 5.0. avg([]) divides 0 by -1 and returns -0.0 (or 0 for ints) instead of raising. So the bad empty-list input is now hidden, and a valid one-element input now fails.
findings.recommendation: Reverting the fix above solves this. Also consider handling empty input explicitly, e.g. `if not xs: raise ValueError("avg() of empty sequence")`.
